title: Installing Packages
description: Add, update, remove, and audit dependencies, and know the difference between production, development, peer, and optional dependencies.

data.text: Installing a package is one command, but choosing *where* it lands in `package.json` decides what ships to production and what breaks your consumers.

rows: Runtime libraries such as react, express, zod
Libraries the host app must provide (react in a component library)
Platform-specific binaries where a missing build is acceptable

data.title: Install into each section
data.content: npm, Yarn, and pnpm use the same flags.
data.code:
npm install express            # dependencies
npm install -D vitest          # devDependencies
npm install -O fsevents        # optionalDependencies
npm install -P react           # peerDependencies (npm 7+)

# Yarn
yarn add express
yarn add --dev vitest
yarn add --peer react

data.text: By default npm writes a caret range such as `^1.2.3`, which allows any minor update. Use `--save-exact` when reproducibility matters more than automatic fixes — common for CLI tools and critical infrastructure packages.

data.title: Save the exact version you tested
CI install: fail instead of silently changing the tree
data.content: `npm ci` deletes node_modules and installs exactly what the lockfile says; it errors if package.json and the lockfile disagree.
data.code:
npm ci                      # CI
npm install                 # local development
yarn install --immutable    # CI (Yarn Berry)

data.title: See what is installed, what is stale, and what is duplicated
data.code:
npm ls react        # why is this version here?
npm outdated        # newer versions available
npm dedupe          # collapse duplicates where possible
npm audit fix       # apply non-breaking security fixes

data.title: Do not delete node_modules to "fix" an error first
data.text: Reinstalling without changing the lockfile rarely helps and hides the real cause. Check `npm ls <pkg>` for duplicate or conflicting versions, then fix the range.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: They want to hear that `dependencies` ship to production while `devDependencies` do not, that peer dependencies are the host app's responsibility, and that CI should run a frozen install rather than `npm install`.

data.title: Audit a project's dependency hygiene
data.description: Open any project you have and answer three questions.
steps: Run npm ls --depth=0 and count direct dependencies.
Group them into runtime and tooling; move any that are miscategorised.
Run npm outdated and pick one safe patch update, then re-run the tests.
data.expectedOutcome: A package.json where each dependency sits in the right section and at least one dependency is deliberately updated and verified.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: The section matters: production installs skip devDependencies.
Peer dependencies are provided by the consumer, not bundled.
Use --save-exact for tools where an unexpected minor release is risky.
npm ci / yarn install --immutable are the CI-safe, lockfile-driven installs.
data.takeaway: Know the four dependency sections cold — it is a favourite interview filter question.
